uncited: This family comprises the fundamental geometric and computational primitives required to construct a volume rendering pipeline.
It addresses the foundational tasks of defining the viewing geometry (rays) and executing the rendering computations efficiently on modern hardware.

It sets itself apart from sibling methods by providing the low-level infrastructure—ray parameterization and parallel execution models—upon which higher-level techniques like surface extraction or light transport are built.
The shared principles of this family are the geometric definition of rays and the parallel execution model.
Rays are defined by an origin $\mathbf{o}$ and a direction $\mathbf{d}$.
The origin is often the camera eye position, but can vary based on the camera model.
Computations are mapped to parallel threads.
Each thread typically processes one or more pixels or samples.
Memory access patterns are optimized for coalescing.
Synchronization is used to manage data dependencies between threads.
The concept of ray generation is rooted in computer graphics since the advent of ray tracing [S2].
Parallel execution primitives have evolved with the rise of GPUs, becoming essential for real-time volume rendering [S1, S3].
